Before committing, I verify memory_31 (day 12, earliest and least mature consolidation, foundational to this action) and memory_86 (day 52, overlapping onboarding claim) since they are jointly the most consequential and least scrutinized inputs to this specific decision—if they conflict or the original signup-simplification result was narrow/confounded, the action should shift. final.rationale: Verification confirms both memories: exp_31 shows signup simplification lifts activation (+9%) and qualified revenue (+4%) on SMB, though with a slight -1% retention dip and no replication outside SMB; exp_86 shows shortened onboarding improves completion (+13%), time-to-value, and retention (+3%). Together these directly address both declining internal metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) with concrete evidence of qualified-revenue-positive outcomes, unlike promotional_pricing (memory_73, unverified, risks a margin race against a competitor with no evidence of durable qualified-revenue gain) or the other candidates which don't address this quarter's specific regressions. I proceed with simplify_onboarding at standard_experiment scale rather than broad_rollout, since the retention dip in exp_31 and its SMB-only replication warrant continued measurement rather than full-scale commitment.
